To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a monoclonal antibody–conjugated iron oxide nanoparticle, which binds to cancer cell surface antigen, can be used in conjunction with externally applied alternating magnetic fields to deliver thermoablational cancer therapy.
the use of mAb-conjugate nanoparticles (bioprobe) given i.v. can be used in conjunction with an externally applied AMF for the delivery of thermoablative cancer cell killing.
we have developed a tumor targeting bioprobe for AMF cancer therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new approach to cancer treatment that combines the targeting properties of monoclonal antibodies with the heating properties of iron oxide particles to provide a new form of cancer therapy.
the development of tumor-targeting bioprobes (111 In-chimeric L-6 monoclonal antibody nanoparticles) for alternating magnetic field cancer therapy.

the use of monoclonal antibodies to target nanoparticles to cancer cells, with the goal of using these targeted nanoparticles in conjunction with externally applied AMFs to deliver thermoablational cancer therapy to the cancer cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of 111In-chimerized L6 (Ch-L6) monocloncal antibody (mAb)-linked iron oxide nanoparticles (bioproves) in concert with an externally applied alternating magnetic fields (AMF) can be used to deliver thermoablitive cancer therapy.

this study showed that the use of mAb-conjugate nanoparticles (bioprobe) given i.v. can escape the intravascular space and bind on the surfaces of cancer cells, so that bioprobe can be used in conjunction with an externally applied AMF for the delivery of cancer therapy.
we have demonstrated the ability of a tumor-specific mAb to deliver iron oxide nanoparticles to a tumor and to induce cell death by heating the nanoparticles using an external AMF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the bioprobes can bind to the tumor cells and that the tumor can be heated to 50°C, and the tumor is necrotic.
the use of mAb-conjugates to iron oxide nanoparticles, with subsequent application of AMF to the tumor, provides a means to deliver targeted cancer therapy.

we have developed an approach for targeted therapy of cancer using nanoparticles linked to monoclonal antibodies that bind to tumor cell surface antigens, and we have shown that the nanoparticles can be used in conjunction with externally applied AMFs to deliver therapeutic heat to tumor sites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bioprobes are a new and promising class of agents for the treatment of cancer.
the bioprobes can target the cancer and that the AMF/bioprobes can be therapeutic.

we have shown that tumor-targeting bioprobes, when given i.v. to athymic mice with human breast cancer, can be used with an externally applied AMF for inductive heating and thermoablative tumor cell killing.
